prompt: A solid has as its base the region bounded by $y = \sqrt{x}$, the $x$-axis and $x = 4$. Every cross-section perpendicular to the $x$-axis is a square. Find the volume of the solid.
hint: At position $x$, the side of the square is the height of the base region there. The area of the square is the side squared.

hints.text: At position $x$, the side of the square is the height of the base region there. The area of the square is the side squared.
The side is $s = \sqrt{x}$, so each slice has area $x$. Add up the slices: $V = \int_0^4 (\sqrt{x})^2 \, dx = \int_0^4 x \, dx$.
The integral is $\left[\frac{x^2}{2}\right]_0^4 = 8$, so the volume is $8$ cubic units.

explanation: Volume by cross-sections is $V = \int_a^b A(x) \, dx$, where $A(x)$ is the area of the slice at $x$.
The side of the square is $\sqrt{x}$, so the area of each slice is $A(x) = x$.
Then $V = \int_0^4 x \, dx = 8$ cubic units. No $\pi$ appears, because these slices are squares, not discs.

alternativeExplanations.title: Compare with the disc version
steps: Rotating the same base about the $x$-axis gives discs of area $\pi x$ and volume $8\pi$.
A square of side $s$ has area $s^2$, while a disc of radius $s$ has area $\pi s^2$ — so the square-slice solid is exactly $\frac{1}{\pi}$ of the disc solid.
